glucose.description: Insulin is released in response to rising blood glucose. Higher glucose triggers more insulin secretion. Chronically elevated glucose with high insulin suggests developing insulin resistance.
HbA1c reflects the average blood glucose level over the past 2-3 months. Elevated glucose consistently leads to higher HbA1c through glycation of hemoglobin.
Glucose and ketones have an inverse relationship. When glucose is low (fasting, keto diet), the liver produces ketone bodies as alternative fuel. High glucose suppresses ketogenesis.
Excess glucose is converted to triglycerides via de novo lipogenesis in the liver. High-carbohydrate diets that raise glucose also tend to raise triglycerides.

insulin.description: Insulin is released in response to rising blood glucose. Higher glucose triggers more insulin secretion. Chronically elevated glucose with high insulin suggests developing insulin resistance.
Insulin promotes triglyceride synthesis and inhibits lipolysis. Hyperinsulinemia drives elevated triglycerides through increased hepatic VLDL production.
Insulin resistance is associated with lower HDL-C. The mechanism involves increased CETP activity and altered lipoprotein metabolism when insulin signaling is impaired.
Insulin reduces renal uric acid excretion. Hyperinsulinemia promotes uric acid reabsorption in the kidneys, often leading to elevated serum uric acid.
In males, insulin resistance can lower testosterone via reduced Leydig cell function. In females with PCOS, hyperinsulinemia drives excess androgen production.
GGT is an independent marker of insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome. Elevated GGT often precedes diabetes diagnosis, reflecting hepatic fat accumulation.
Chronic low-grade inflammation (elevated CRP) is associated with insulin resistance. Adipose tissue inflammation produces cytokines that impair insulin signaling.

hba1c.description: HbA1c reflects the average blood glucose level over the past 2-3 months. Elevated glucose consistently leads to higher HbA1c through glycation of hemoglobin.

ketones.description: Glucose and ketones have an inverse relationship. When glucose is low (fasting, keto diet), the liver produces ketone bodies as alternative fuel. High glucose suppresses ketogenesis.

tsh.description: TSH and free T4 have a log-linear inverse relationship. When T4 drops, the pituitary increases TSH production. Elevated TSH with low FT4 indicates hypothyroidism.
TSH rises when T3 is insufficient. T3 is the active thyroid hormone. Poor T4-to-T3 conversion can cause elevated TSH with normal FT4 but low FT3.

ft4.description: TSH and free T4 have a log-linear inverse relationship. When T4 drops, the pituitary increases TSH production. Elevated TSH with low FT4 indicates hypothyroidism.
T3 is produced primarily by peripheral conversion of T4. They generally move together, but conversion can be impaired by selenium deficiency, inflammation, or stress.

ft3.description: TSH rises when T3 is insufficient. T3 is the active thyroid hormone. Poor T4-to-T3 conversion can cause elevated TSH with normal FT4 but low FT3.
T3 is produced primarily by peripheral conversion of T4. They generally move together, but conversion can be impaired by selenium deficiency, inflammation, or stress.

calcium.description: Vitamin D enhances intestinal calcium absorption. Deficiency leads to reduced calcium absorption, triggering PTH release to maintain serum calcium by pulling from bones.

magnesium.description: Magnesium is required for the Na/K-ATPase pump that maintains potassium balance. Magnesium deficiency can cause refractory hypokalemia that does not respond to potassium supplementation alone.

potassium.description: Magnesium is required for the Na/K-ATPase pump that maintains potassium balance. Magnesium deficiency can cause refractory hypokalemia that does not respond to potassium supplementation alone.

creatinine.description: eGFR is calculated from creatinine (and sometimes cystatin C). As kidney function declines, creatinine rises and eGFR falls. Note: creatine supplementation raises creatinine without affecting kidney function.

vitamin_d.description: Vitamin D enhances intestinal calcium absorption. Deficiency leads to reduced calcium absorption, triggering PTH release to maintain serum calcium by pulling from bones.

iron.description: Ferritin reflects total body iron stores. Low ferritin indicates iron depletion even before serum iron drops. However, ferritin is also an acute phase reactant and rises with inflammation.
Iron is essential for hemoglobin synthesis. Iron deficiency leads to decreased hemoglobin production and eventually iron-deficiency anemia.
Transferrin saturation indicates what percentage of iron-binding sites are occupied. It reflects current iron availability more acutely than ferritin.

total_cholesterol.description: LDL-C is the largest component of total cholesterol. Total cholesterol rises primarily when LDL-C increases, though HDL and VLDL also contribute.

ldl_c.description: Each LDL particle carries one ApoB molecule. LDL-C and ApoB generally move together, but can diverge when LDL particles are small and dense (more particles per unit of cholesterol).
LDL and HDL cholesterol should be interpreted together. The ratio reflects cardiovascular risk better than either alone. HDL performs reverse cholesterol transport.
LDL-C is the largest component of total cholesterol. Total cholesterol rises primarily when LDL-C increases, though HDL and VLDL also contribute.

hdl_c.description: Insulin resistance is associated with lower HDL-C. The mechanism involves increased CETP activity and altered lipoprotein metabolism when insulin signaling is impaired.
LDL and HDL cholesterol should be interpreted together. The ratio reflects cardiovascular risk better than either alone. HDL performs reverse cholesterol transport.
High triglycerides are strongly associated with low HDL-C. This dyslipidemia pattern is a hallmark of metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance.

triglycerides.description: Excess glucose is converted to triglycerides via de novo lipogenesis in the liver. High-carbohydrate diets that raise glucose also tend to raise triglycerides.
Insulin promotes triglyceride synthesis and inhibits lipolysis. Hyperinsulinemia drives elevated triglycerides through increased hepatic VLDL production.
High triglycerides are strongly associated with low HDL-C. This dyslipidemia pattern is a hallmark of metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance.

apob.description: Each LDL particle carries one ApoB molecule. LDL-C and ApoB generally move together, but can diverge when LDL particles are small and dense (more particles per unit of cholesterol).
Lp(a) particles carry one ApoB each and contribute to the total ApoB count. Elevated Lp(a) can make ApoB appear high even when LDL particle count is normal.

lpa.description: Lp(a) particles carry one ApoB each and contribute to the total ApoB count. Elevated Lp(a) can make ApoB appear high even when LDL particle count is normal.

hs_crp.description: Both ferritin and CRP rise during inflammation. Elevated ferritin with elevated CRP may reflect acute phase response rather than true iron overload. Interpret ferritin in context of inflammatory markers.

Both are markers of systemic inflammation. CRP is produced by the liver in response to IL-6, while elevated WBC indicates immune system activation. Chronic elevation of both suggests ongoing inflammatory processes.
Chronic low-grade inflammation (elevated CRP) is associated with insulin resistance. Adipose tissue inflammation produces cytokines that impair insulin signaling.

vitamin_b12.description: B12 is a cofactor for methionine synthase, which converts homocysteine to methionine. B12 deficiency leads to homocysteine accumulation, increasing cardiovascular risk.
B12 and folate work together in the methionine cycle and DNA synthesis. Deficiency of either can cause megaloblastic anemia. B12 deficiency can mask folate deficiency and vice versa.

folate.description: Folate donates the methyl group needed to convert homocysteine back to methionine. Low folate is one of the most common causes of elevated homocysteine.
B12 and folate work together in the methionine cycle and DNA synthesis. Deficiency of either can cause megaloblastic anemia. B12 deficiency can mask folate deficiency and vice versa.

testosterone.description: SHBG binds testosterone, reducing its bioavailability. High SHBG can cause symptoms of low testosterone despite normal total testosterone. Free testosterone is what matters clinically.
Free testosterone is the unbound, bioactive fraction. It depends on both total testosterone and SHBG levels. Low free testosterone with normal total may indicate high SHBG.
In males, insulin resistance can lower testosterone via reduced Leydig cell function. In females with PCOS, hyperinsulinemia drives excess androgen production.
Testosterone is converted to estradiol by aromatase enzyme, primarily in adipose tissue. Higher body fat can shift the ratio toward estradiol. Both are important for bone health in both sexes.

estradiol.description: Testosterone is converted to estradiol by aromatase enzyme, primarily in adipose tissue. Higher body fat can shift the ratio toward estradiol. Both are important for bone health in both sexes.

wbc.description: Both are markers of systemic inflammation. CRP is produced by the liver in response to IL-6, while elevated WBC indicates immune system activation. Chronic elevation of both suggests ongoing inflammatory processes.

hemoglobin.description: Iron is essential for hemoglobin synthesis. Iron deficiency leads to decreased hemoglobin production and eventually iron-deficiency anemia.

homocysteine.description: B12 is a cofactor for methionine synthase, which converts homocysteine to methionine. B12 deficiency leads to homocysteine accumulation, increasing cardiovascular risk.
Folate donates the methyl group needed to convert homocysteine back to methionine. Low folate is one of the most common causes of elevated homocysteine.

free_testosterone.description: Free testosterone is the unbound, bioactive fraction. It depends on both total testosterone and SHBG levels. Low free testosterone with normal total may indicate high SHBG.

shbg.description: SHBG binds testosterone, reducing its bioavailability. High SHBG can cause symptoms of low testosterone despite normal total testosterone. Free testosterone is what matters clinically.

alt.description: Both are liver enzymes released during hepatocyte damage. ALT is more liver-specific, while AST is also found in muscle and heart. Their ratio helps distinguish liver conditions.
Both rise with liver stress. GGT is particularly sensitive to alcohol use and biliary obstruction. Elevated GGT with normal ALT may indicate oxidative stress or medication effects.

ast.description: Both are liver enzymes released during hepatocyte damage. ALT is more liver-specific, while AST is also found in muscle and heart. Their ratio helps distinguish liver conditions.

ggt.description: Both rise with liver stress. GGT is particularly sensitive to alcohol use and biliary obstruction. Elevated GGT with normal ALT may indicate oxidative stress or medication effects.
GGT is an independent marker of insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome. Elevated GGT often precedes diabetes diagnosis, reflecting hepatic fat accumulation.

egfr.description: eGFR is calculated from creatinine (and sometimes cystatin C). As kidney function declines, creatinine rises and eGFR falls. Note: creatine supplementation raises creatinine without affecting kidney function.
Elevated uric acid is associated with declining kidney function. The kidneys excrete uric acid, so impaired filtration leads to accumulation. Uric acid may also directly damage renal tubules.

uric_acid.description: Insulin reduces renal uric acid excretion. Hyperinsulinemia promotes uric acid reabsorption in the kidneys, often leading to elevated serum uric acid.
Elevated uric acid is associated with declining kidney function. The kidneys excrete uric acid, so impaired filtration leads to accumulation. Uric acid may also directly damage renal tubules.
